column7: STARTUP-GUARD-TAILS-1 (docs/design/trigger-rowdigest.md, Findings). The secret_nodes cache-epoch trigger had the owner-level exposure the role-permission generation triggers had: the server database role could replace keyorix_secret_nodes_bump_cache_epoch() with a body that keeps OLD.cache_epoch, re-create the trigger as AFTER UPDATE, or disable it around a direct write and let the next boot re-enable it, and warm replicas kept serving the pre-change row (a suspended secret read as active). The periodic trigger integrity check now covers this trigger and function (definition, pinned search_path, pg_trigger/pg_proc xmin), and on a difference logs, counts keyorix_secret_node_cache_epoch_tamper_total, repairs and moves cache_epoch on every live row so every replica misses. The installer no longer rewrites a correct function on boot. Also _DisabledTriggerReenabledByBootIsFlushed_Postgres, _ReplicaTriggerConvergedByBootIsFlushed_Postgres, _DroppedFunctionReinstalledByBootIsFlushed_Postgres, _DisableWriteEnableInOneTransactionIsFlushed_Postgres, _TriggerRecreatedAsAfterIsRestored_Postgres, _FailedRepairIsRetriedNotAdopted_Postgres; installer half TestSecretNodeCacheEpoch_EnsureLeavesCorrectFunctionRowAlone_Postgres and _EnsureRestoresRecreatedTrigger_Postgres (red on main by behaviour). Residual: one interval for deliberate DDL; a superuser below SQL is not detected.
